fields.description: Named build agent image from the platform catalog. Not a raw image reference - keeps step code portable and centrally patchable. Still required even when `script` is omitted, since unit tests always run inside this image regardless of build strategy.

Build script the platform runs inside the agent image before packaging. Must be bash. Omit entirely for teams doing the whole build inside a multi-stage Containerfile - the separate build-source stage is skipped and BuildKit builds `containerfile` directly. No default: presence/absence is the switch, so it can't silently mean 'skip' via an unrelated typo.

Path to a multi-stage Containerfile BuildKit builds directly - only consulted when build.script is omitted. "Containerfile" (not "Dockerfile") is this platform's deliberate, vendor-neutral term for the same OCI-buildable file format - BuildKit itself has no opinion on the name, and it's the same file whichever name your repo uses.

Persistent dependency-download cache for build-source (npm's package cache / Maven's local repository, not node_modules/target itself - see docs/cicd-yaml-reference.md). No `type` field: derived from `agent`'s prefix (nodejs-* -> npm, openjdk-* -> maven), not a second, redundantly-declarable field. One shared directory per tool, never keyed by a lockfile hash - npm's cache is content-addressed and Maven's local repository is laid out per exact version, so neither can serve a stale package and a dependency bump only fetches what changed. Shared by build-source and (npm/yarn only) run-tests' unit-test step. A no-op (logged, not an error) for agents without cache support yet (python-*/go-1.22). Teams with no build.script (whole build inside a multi-stage Dockerfile) get layer caching for free from BuildKit instead.

T-shirt size for this app's own cache PVC (small=1Gi, medium=2.5Gi, large=5Gi, xlarge=8Gi - same dictionary as the old cd-pipelines-user Helm chart's buildSpec.cacheSize). One PVC per app, specifically so this can vary per app. Chosen at onboarding time, not resizable live afterward - a kind cluster's default storage class has allowVolumeExpansion: false, so changing this later means recreating the PVC (and losing its cached content), not a live resize.

T-shirt size for the ephemeral `source` workspace every stage's PipelineRun gets (small=2Gi, medium=5Gi, large=10Gi, xlarge=20Gi). This is the checked-out git repo plus build.script's own output plus the image build context - distinct from build.cache (a separate, persistent, per-app dependency-download cache). Exists because a large build can genuinely fill this workspace's disk ('no space left on device'), not because of anything cache-related. Not per-stage: one size applies to every stage's source workspace for this app (build/test/deploy/release all declare the same `source` workspace shape), since build is normally the only stage large enough to need this, and a single per-app knob is simpler than one per stage. Not resizable live - each PipelineRun's workspace is a fresh, ephemeral volumeClaimTemplate-backed PVC (unlike build.cache's persistent one), so a size change just takes effect on the next run, nothing to migrate.

fields.description: Lowercase letters, digits and '-', starting with a letter, at most 31 characters. Also used in the environment's namespace name.

ground: deploys on every push. flight: deploys only through a release PR and its guardrails. For a cloud target (aws-ecs, aws-lambda, azure-container-apps) a flight environment is approved by a release pin PR on the source repo (glidepath/releases/<env>.yaml, ADR-0020) and sets no cluster.

Flight only, and only when the environment runs on a different cluster than the app's own (a cluster name from the platform cluster registry). A Ground environment cannot set it yet: Ground environments on other clusters are a future feature (docs/admin/known-gaps.md).

Marks the environment that serves real users and real data (ADR-0024). Must be a Flight environment, and for a Kubernetes target its cluster must be an upper cluster in the platform cluster registry (one nothing below it can write to, changed only through reviewed merges).

deployment = native k8s Deployment rollout; rollout = Argo Rollouts (canary/blue-green). Rollout support has since landed and is the only strategy actually implemented (deploy-manifests.yaml manages an Argo Rollout unconditionally via the airframe-application chart - confirmed live, 2026-09-17): `deployment` is schema-valid but has NO effect - nothing renders a plain Deployment anymore. This is the reverse of this field's original meaning when it was first added (rollout was the future, unimplemented option then); kept as a two-value enum, default flipped, so an existing cicd.yaml that explicitly sets `strategy: deployment` still validates rather than breaking, even though it no longer describes real behavior.

Where the deploy/release stages write the machine-owned release record (release.image, releaseTracking) - see hangar/docs/autopilot/release-file-split.md (D9/AF-5). Exactly one `{env}` placeholder, substituted with the target environment name, matching deploy-manifests.yaml's own `${ENV}` variable. Schema-only today: no Task reads this field yet - deploy-manifests.yaml and open-release-pr.yaml still hardcode `platform/envs/${ENV}.yaml`/the gitops repo's `values.yaml`. The field exists now so the Airframe onboarding scaffold can start setting it (`airframe/envs/{env}.release.yaml`, once that directory exists) without a second wave of per-app cicd.yaml edits later. Default names a new, not-yet-existing Glidepath-owned path (`glidepath/`, distinct from Airframe's `platform/`/`airframe/` directory) for an app onboarded without an Airframe chart to layer a release file over - per the design doc's own default-path decision, not an existing convention anywhere else in this repo.
fields.why: The file a release writes; a wrong path deploys nowhere or somewhere else.

fields.description: Where deploy.yaml's `deploy` stage actually deploys to. k8s-rollout (default) is the only target every existing app uses - deploy-manifests.yaml, Argo Rollouts via airframe-application, zero behavior change for an app that doesn't set this. The three cloud targets (added 2026-10-03/04) each require a matching config block below plus this app's own `secrets:` entries for cloud credentials (see docs/admin/app-secrets.md) - none are live-verified against a real account, see docs/admin/known-gaps.md. All three resolve correctly even for a git-rooted deploy (no build/test in that run) - resolve-deploy-target.yaml clones cicd.yaml directly via the GitHub App token broker in that case, rather than trusting an unpopulated config-json. - aws-ecs (deploy-ecs.yaml): registers a new ECS task-definition revision and updates the named service. Requires `deploy.ecs` and an Airframe AwsEcsTarget for the service: the deploy copies the image into the target's ECR repository and assumes the target's deploy role with a web identity; no AWS secret is used. - aws-lambda (deploy-lambda.yaml): updates an existing function's container image. Requires `deploy.lambda` and an Airframe AwsLambdaTarget for the function: the deploy assumes the target's role with a web identity, and no AWS secret is used (docs/admin/cloud-deploy-identity.md). Hard AWS constraint: image-repo must resolve to an Amazon ECR URI - Lambda cannot pull from an external registry like ghcr.io. - azure-container-apps (deploy-azure-container-apps.yaml): updates an existing Container App's image to a new revision. Requires `deploy.azureContainerApps` and secrets `azure-client-id`/`azure-client-secret`/`azure-tenant-id`.

Shift-left notifications from sast-scan/image-scan the moment each real scan produces a result, separate from the general build/test/deploy/release pass-fail notification above (which stays on whenever slack.enabled is true). Only takes effect when slack.enabled is also true. Defaults on (matching the pipeline's own default real-scan behavior), but an app that finds these too frequent/verbose can turn just this off without losing the general per-stage notifications.

Sends the same build/test/deploy/release pass-fail notification as notifications.slack into Backstage's own Notifications plugin (broadcast to every Backstage user, viewable in Tower's Notifications tab), instead of/in addition to Slack. Independent toggle - either target can be on, off, or both. Requires the cluster's glidepath-catalog chart to have backstageBaseUrl and a glidepath-backstage-notify token secret configured (see docs/admin/notifications.md); a cluster without that setup skips silently.

Also the default for `key` below, so the common case (the name you want to use here already matches the name it has in your backend store) needs only this one field.

fields.description: Preferred explicit shape: git triggers evaluate branch/path filters; event triggers use the broker CDEvents path and the event field.

Explicit event identifier for the root trigger. For git sources this is the Git event kind; for event sources it is the CDEvents event type. No release.created - confirmed live that Pipelines-as-Code has no support for GitHub 'release' webhooks at all (any version): a real delivery came back '{"status":200,"message":"skipping non supported event"}', filtered out before PaC's own annotation matching ever runs, so no Trigger config could ever make this fire. Use 'tag' instead - publishing a GitHub Release also creates the underlying tag, which fires a real, working push event.
Legacy shorthand for the git-trigger form. Newer configs should use source+event.
Regex the pushed tag's name must match, required when event is 'tag' (e.g. 'v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'). See deliver-onboarding-files.yaml's generate_flow_file.

Only meaningful on a test step with role test or execute. Overrides the top-level test.name for this specific step - needed when a flow has more than one test step (they'd otherwise be indistinguishable). Falls back to test.name when omitted; one of the two must resolve to a value, since a TestWorkflow run always needs a name. Not valid with role check-ride (that workflow's name is the platform's). Not called `name` - that field below is the deploy/release target name, a different concept.

Only meaningful on a test step. What kind of thing the step is (docs/admin/testing.md). test (default): the team's own TestWorkflow from glidepath/<testName>.yaml - results recorded and shown, the next stage chains on them. execute: an action, not a test (clear a cache, seed a fixture) - same workflow source and chaining, no test evidence expected. check-ride: the standard the release depends on - runs <app>-check-ride from the shared check-rides repository (synced into Testkube by Argo CD, never applied from this repo), takes no testName, at most one per flow; its passing run is the evidence the qa release gate reads.
Only meaningful on a test step. false: a failed run is recorded as failed but does not stop the flow - the next stage still runs. For best-effort execute steps. A check-ride step is always required.

Only meaningful on a test step. How long the stage waits for the TestWorkflow execution to reach a terminal status (Ns, Nm or Nh). Past it the outcome is `timeout` and the step fails; Testkube's own step timeouts inside the workflow still apply.

Only meaningful (and required) on a gitops-image-bump step: the gitops repo (by name, e.g. 'gitops-cluster-example-prod') to open the image-bump PR against. Unlike release's gitops-<app-name> convention, this stage is for a hand-deployed singleton/cluster-config component whose manifests don't live in a per-app gitops repo, so the target repo must be named explicitly. Requires an extra Repository CR granting this app's CI namespace write access - see platformIdentity.extraGitopsRepos in the tenant identity.yaml (not this repo's cicd.yaml, since it's a trust/authorization grant the app owner doesn't self-serve).

Only meaningful (and required) on a gitops-image-bump step: path within gitopsRepo to a plain Kubernetes manifest (not airframe-application Helm values.yaml) whose first container's image field gets patched, e.g. '60-backstage/backstage/deployment.yaml'.

gates.name: sast
gates.description: Static analysis (Semgrep) of the promoted commit's source

gates.name: image-scan
gates.description: Vulnerability scan (Trivy) of the promoted image

gates.name: provenance
gates.description: Commit signature (gitsign, or a GitHub PR merge by an allowed login) + SLSA provenance (Conforma)

gates.name: values
gates.description: Values-file validation (strict keys, component XRD specs, helm template) by the validator image

gates.name: itsm
gates.description: An approved or scheduled change request for this release in the change tool (ServiceNow, or any tool behind the webhook adapter)

gates.name: api-compat
gates.description: API compatibility - the promoted image's signed API spec (cicd.yaml api.spec) diffed against the spec of the image the target environment runs, with the operations each breaking change touches and whether they are in use

gates.name: qa
gates.description: A passing, recent check ride from the shared check-rides repository, attested on the promoted image

gates.name: policy-validation
gates.description: The release's rendered manifests evaluated offline (Kyverno CLI) against the target cluster's admission policies (ValidatingPolicy, ClusterPolicy, ValidatingAdmissionPolicy) from its GitOps repo

run.succeeded: The PipelineRun finished and every task passed.
run.failed: A task failed or the run timed out.
run.unknown: Tekton Results reported no status Glidepath recognises.

release.proposed: The release PR is open on gitops-<app>.
release.merged: The release PR merged; Argo CD has not reported yet.
release.sync-failed: Argo CD's sync failed. Not terminal; a retry can move it on.
release.progressing: The Rollout is progressing or paused.
release.superseded: A newer release of the same app, environment and cluster replaced it. Terminal.
release.rolled-back: A rollback release naming this one turned healthy. Terminal.
release.closed: The release PR closed without merging. Terminal.

knownFailures.match: cicd\.yaml not found|Every app repo needs a cicd\.yaml
knownFailures.hint: Add cicd.yaml at the repo root; Airframe scaffolds one for a new app.

knownFailures.match: cicd\.yaml failed schema validation
knownFailures.hint: Run `glidepath validate cicd.yaml`; it names the field and the rule.

knownFailures.match: which deploy\.environments replaced
knownFailures.hint: List each environment once under deploy.environments, in promotion order, with tier ground or flight.

knownFailures.match: no space left on device
knownFailures.hint: Raise build.sourceVolume.size one step (small, medium, large, xlarge).

knownFailures.match: build\.script '.*' \(from cicd\.yaml\) not found
knownFailures.hint: Point build.script at a file in the repo, or remove it to use the agent's default build.

knownFailures.match: names no workflow: .* does not exist in this commit
knownFailures.hint: Add glidepath/<testName>.yaml (a Testkube TestWorkflow), or fix test.name or the step's testName.

knownFailures.match: no check ride for .*: TestWorkflow .* does not exist
knownFailures.hint: Add apps/<app>/check-ride.yaml to the check-rides repository. An app team can't fix this in its own repo.

knownFailures.match: was not synced by Argo CD \(no argocd\.argoproj\.io/tracking-id\)
knownFailures.hint: A check ride must come from the check-rides repository, never be applied by hand.

knownFailures.match: has no linux/.* image - check build\.platforms|is a linux/.* image, but the Lambda function is
knownFailures.hint: Add the target's architecture to build.platforms.

knownFailures.match: not running as glidepath-cloud-deployer|could not assume .*:
knownFailures.hint: The cloud target creates the deploy role; check the target XR is Ready. Not a cicd.yaml change.

knownFailures.match: deploy\.target is (aws-ecs|aws-lambda|azure-container-apps) but
knownFailures.hint: Fill the deploy block the target's status.cicd publishes. A human owns these fields.

knownFailures.match: cluster '.*' has no entry in the glidepath cluster-registry
knownFailures.hint: The environment names a cluster the platform doesn't know. A human owns deploy.environments[].cluster.

knownFailures.match: rollout .* is Degraded on
knownFailures.hint: The new version failed its rollout. Read the Rollout's analysis, then fix the code or roll back.

knownFailures.match: timed out waiting for rollout .* to run .* Healthy
knownFailures.hint: The rollout never became healthy. Check the pods and the canary analysis.

knownFailures.match: sibling guardrail '.*' completed with conclusion
knownFailures.hint: Another release gate failed first; fix that one.

knownFailures.match: is in state .* with approval .* - not approved or scheduled
knownFailures.hint: The change request needs approval in the change tool before the release can merge.

knownFailures.match: no verified slsaprovenance attestations found|no attestations found for
knownFailures.hint: The image has no signed provenance; it was not built by Glidepath, or Chains has not signed it yet.

knownFailures.match: now resolves to .*, not the pinned
knownFailures.hint: The tag was pushed again after approval. Release the digest that was approved.

knownFailures.match: fatal: repository '.*' not found
knownFailures.hint: Glidepath could not clone the repository. Check it exists under that name (a renamed or deleted repo) and that the platform's GitHub credential can still read it. An app team can't fix this in cicd.yaml.

knownFailures.match: TestWorkflowExecution .* finished with status: failed
knownFailures.hint: The app's tests ran and failed. Read the execution in Tower's Tests view for the failing case; fix the code or the test.

knownFailures.match: image-scan: trivy found [0-9]+ HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerabilities
knownFailures.hint: The image has HIGH or CRITICAL vulnerabilities. Rebuild on a patched base image or update the listed packages; the scan step's log lists each CVE. Don't turn the scan off.
